<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and the README, the MoviePilot project appears to be a full‐stack application (with the frontend being in a separate repository) that provides a FastAPI-based backend. Its purpose is to handle media-related functionalities (such as downloads, subscriptions, media searches, integration with media services, etc.) while keeping a core automation focus. Here are detailed guidelines for drawing the most accurate and detailed system design diagram for MoviePilot:

1. Identify the Main Components:
   • Frontend: Although not included in this repository, note that a separate Vue3-based frontend (MoviePilot-Frontend) interfaces with this backend.
   • API Layer: This is clearly represented by the “app/api/” directory with multiple endpoints (login, media, download, dashboard, etc.). It handles HTTP/REST requests and responses.
   • Business Logic (Chain): The “app/chain/” directory encapsulates step-by-step business flows, mapping closely to API endpoints. It acts as a mediator to process requests and trigger actions.
   • Core Modules: Found in “app/core/”, this contains key components such as configuration management, caching, event handling, plugin management, and metadata extraction. It represents common services used by the entire application.
   • Database Layer: All operations related to data persistence are grouped under “app/db/”. It includes database initialization, models (for users, downloads, subscriptions, etc.), and operational scripts. Make sure to include a depiction of how models interact with business logic.
   • Helper Utilities: “app/helper/” provides utility functions for common tasks like file downloading, cookie handling, and formatting – these support multiple layers.
   • Modules / External Integrations: The “app/modules/” directory is extensive and includes integrations with various external services (e.g., Douban, Bangumi, Emby, Plex, The Movie DB, etc.). This shows that the backend is built for extendability, with each module handling specific integration or functionality.
   • Plugins System: Both “app/plugins/” and parts of the “app/core/plugin.py” reveal that the system is designed to be easily extended.
   • Startup and Scheduling: “app/startup/” and other files like “app/scheduler.py” indicate that there is an orchestration layer to initialize modules and schedule recurring tasks.
   • Utility and Configuration Files: These include environment and configuration files in the “config/” folder, Docker files, and build scripts that are key to deployment and runtime environment setup.
   
2. Define Relationships and Interactions:
   • The Frontend (Vue3) communicates with the FastAPI-based backend through the API endpoints.
   • The API layer receives requests from the frontend and routes them to the business logic (chain) layer.
   • The Chain layer processes these requests by invoking operations in core services, performing validation, triggering helper functions, and interfacing with external modules.
   • Database interactions (CRUD operations) are handled via the “app/db/” layer, with models being used by both the business chain and the API.
   • The Plugins and Modules systems interact with both the core and chain layers to extend functionality for specific external services.
   • Utility functions in “app/helper/” and “app/utils/” are used across multiple layers to handle common operations like file management, network communications, and security (e.g., encryption or two-factor authentication).

3. Highlight Architectural Patterns and Design Principles:
   • Separation of Concerns: Different directories separate API routing, business logic, core services, database operations, integrations, and utilities.
   • Modularity: The “app/modules/” and “app/plugins/” directories show a highly modular design for extensibility and maintainability.
   • Clean API Design: The FastAPI-based endpoints encapsulated in “app/api/” follow RESTful principles for clear interaction boundaries.
   • Dependency Injection & Initialization: The startup scripts (found under “app/startup/”) suggest an initialization phase where various modules and plugins are loaded.
   • Containerization: Use of Docker (Dockerfile, .dockerignore) indicates that the project supports containerized deployments.
   
4. Relevant Technologies, Frameworks, & Libraries:
   • Backend Framework: FastAPI
   • Frontend Technology: Vue3 (separate repository)
   • Database: Likely an SQL/ORM based on the structured “models” directories (precise tech not directly specified but indicated by oper and models design)
   • External Integrations: Several modules indicate integration with services such as Douban, TMDB, TheTVDB, Plex, Emby, qbittorrent, Transmission, etc.
   • Containerization Tools: Docker and related configuration files.
   • Workflow & Scheduling Libraries: Evidenced by “app/scheduler.py” and “app/startup/workflow_initializer.py”

5. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram:
   • For a Full-Stack Application: Emphasize the clear separation between the Vue3 frontend and the FastAPI backend. Use a two-tier layout where the frontend sends requests to API endpoints.
   • Break Down the Backend into the Identified Components:
       - Draw boxes for “API Layer”, “Business Logic (Chain)”, “Core Services”, “Database”, “Modules/Plugins”, “Helper/Utils”, and “Startup/Scheduler”.
       - Connect these with directional arrows showing the data flow:
         • API → Chain (showing request handling flow)
         • Chain → Core (for configuration, caching, etc.)
         • Chain/Core → Database (to illustrate CRUD operations)
         • Chain/Core → Modules/External Services (For integrations)
         • Startup → API/Chain/Modules (show initialization process)
   • Use color-coding or different shapes to differentiate between:
       - Service components (e.g., API vs. Business Logic vs. Database).
       - External integrations versus internal processing logic.

6. Instruct the Principal Software Engineer to Include:
   • Clear Labels: Each component should be clearly named to reflect its directory (e.g., "app/api (FastAPI Endpoints)", "app/chain (Business Workflows)", "app/db (Database Models & Operations)", "app/modules (External Service Integrations)").
   • Directional Arrows: Use arrows to indicate data flow—for instance, how API requests traverse to the business logic, then further to the database or external modules.
   • Visual Differentiators: Use colors, line styles, or shapes (e.g., rectangles for core modules, cylinders for the database, hexagons for external integrations) to easily visualize the separation of concerns.
   • Detailed Annotations: Include notes on important design principles such as modularity, extensibility with plugins, and how containerization (via Docker) supports deployment.

7. Final Tips:
   • Don’t overcomplicate: While it is best to separate the project into as many components as your file tree indicates, make sure to layer the diagram logically so that each layer’s responsibility is clearly isolated.
   • Include Deployment and Infrastructure: Optionally note external elements such as Docker and Nginx (nginx.conf) to show how requests might be routed in production.
   • Maintain Readability: Given MoviePilot’s extensive modular structure, ensure that the diagram remains readable by possibly dividing it into sub-diagrams (e.g., one for API & request flow, another for system integrations).

Following these detailed instructions will help you produce an accurate system design diagram that fully captures the architecture of MoviePilot, emphasizing its modular, extensible, and full-stack nature.
</explanation>
